text: The applicant was born in 1955.
The applicant lives in Yerevan.
The applicant was represented by Ms L. Sahakyan, a lawyer practising in Yerevan.
The applicant was represented by Mr E. Varosyan, a lawyer practising in Yerevan.
The applicant was represented by Mr A. Ghazaryan, a non-practising lawyer.
The Government were represented by their Agent, Mr G. Kostanyan.
The Government were subsequently represented by Mr Y. Kirakosyan, Representative of the Republic of Armenia to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
The applicant was at the material time the Deputy General Prosecutor of Armenia.
The applicant had occupied the post of Deputy General Prosecutor of Armenia since 17 January 2006.
The applicant held the rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.
In the past, the applicant had occupied different high-level posts, including the post of Military Prosecutor of Armenia.
On 19 February 2008 a presidential election was held in Armenia.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: One of the main contenders in the 19 February 2008 presidential election was the then Prime Minister, Mr Sargsyan, representing the ruling party.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: One of the main contenders in the 19 February 2008 presidential election was the main opposition candidate, Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: Mr Ter-Petrosyan announced that the 19 February 2008 presidential election had not been free and fair.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: Several hundred demonstrators stayed in the Freedom Square area around the clock, having set up a camp.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: On 22 February 2008 the applicant made a speech at the rally held at Freedom Square.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant expressed his support for Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant criticised the conduct of the presidential election, alleging various types of irregularities.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant called on those gathered not to give up and to stand by their votes.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant said that rule of law had to be finally established in Armenia.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: The applicant alleged that, following his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the authorities started persecuting him and his family members.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: On 22 February 2008, the same date as the applicant's speech at Freedom Square, the General Prosecutor applied to the President of Armenia seeking to have the applicant dismissed.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: The General Prosecutor's application to the President of Armenia sought the applicant's dismissal on the ground that the applicant had participated in a rally and made a political speech, thereby violating the law which required prosecutors to maintain political neutrality and not to engage in political activities.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree dismissing the applicant from the post of Deputy General Prosecutor.
section_path: I. THE 19 FEBRUARY 2008 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION AND THE POST-ELECTION EVENTS

text: On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree depriving the applicant of his rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.

text: According to the applicant, on 23 February 2008 at around 10 p.m. the applicant, his brother V.J., and four others had been travelling from Ejmiatsin to Yerevan in two cars.

text: According to the applicant, after stopping at the intersection near Argavand village, the applicant and his companions had been attacked by a group of masked and armed persons.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, the masked and armed persons had crashed their unmarked vehicle into the front of the applicant's car.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: According to the applicant, the masked and armed persons had come out of their vehicle and, firing their guns, had surrounded the applicant's car.
section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

section_path: II. THE CRIMINAL PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE APPLICANT

text: For a summary of the relevant domestic law and relevant international materials, see Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia (no. 23086/08) and Ara Harutyunyan v. Armenia (no. 629/11, §§ 30-37, 20 October 2016).

A number of provisions of domestic law and extracts from international materials not quoted in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia (no. 23086/08) or Ara Harutyunyan v. Armenia (no. 629/11) are set out in the relevant legal framework section of this judgment.

Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (2003), as in force at the material time, provided that usurpation of State power, namely actions aimed at violent seizure of State power or its violent retention in violation of the Constitution, as well as violent overthrow of the constitutional order of Armenia or violent breach of the territorial integrity of Armenia, was punishable by imprisonment for a period from ten to fifteen years.

Article 90 § 1(3) of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure (1999), as in force at the material time, provided that a judge is obliged to recuse himself if he is aware of facts or circumstances capable of raising a reasonable doubt as regards his impartiality in a particular case.

Article 90 § 1(3) of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure (1999) provided that grounds for recusal include cases where a judge or his spouse or a person having kinship with him of up to the third degree may reasonably become (or has reasons to believe that he will become) a participant in the proceedings or has participated in the proceedings at a lower instance as a judge or as a participant in the proceedings.

Article 90 § 1(3) of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure (1999) provided that a person's children, parents, sisters and brothers are considered as having kinship of the first degree with him, within the meaning of that Article.
